title: The 6 Skincare Lessons Every Middle-Aged Man Should Know (and the Super Affordable Products to Buy) - Esquire
text:
The 6 Skincare Lessons Every Middle-Aged Man Should Know (and the Super Affordable Products to Buy) In 2026, young men are generally on top of their skincare. But in the before times, a splash of cold water to the face was the extent of most morning regimens. That’s probably why so many middle-aged guys find themselves with dried-out, sun-damaged skin that isn’t quite where they want it to be. The good news is that it’s never too late to pick up good habits.

With that in mind, we asked six of the glowiest people we know to share the products they reach for every day – and the lessons they’ve learned along the way.

But in the before times, a splash of cold water to the face was the extent of most morning regimens. That’s probably why so many middle-aged guys find themselves with dried-out, sun-damaged skin that isn’t quite where they want it to be. The good news is that it’s never too late to pick up good habits. With that in mind, we asked six of the glowiest people we know to share the products they reach for every day – and the lessons they’ve learned along the way. 1 YOUR STUBBLE COMES AT A COST 1 YOUR STUBBLE COMES AT A COST £8 at LookFantastic Caroline Hirons, aesthetician and writer: "Men’s skin is slightly thicker, and a high majority of men shave daily, which can cause its own set of problems if not done properly. Using the right kit and products is important: shaving oils, facial shaving products, post-shave moisturisers… A lot of men with a heavier beard would also benefit from using a daily acid exfoliator to prevent ingrown hairs.” “Skin Rules” by Caroline Hirons is out now 2 INVEST IN KOREAN PRODUCTS 2 INVEST IN KOREAN PRODUCTS £2 at Cult Beauty Saul Nash, menswear designer: "“Korean skincare is everything. I use Reedle Shot 100 masks — I love them and they leave my skin glowing. I do think it’s important, though, not to trouble your skin too much — I have combination [different conditions across the face] to oily skin, so I try not to touch my face a lot or put too many products on it.” Advertisement - Continue Reading Below 3 SKINCARE DOESN’T STOP AT BEDTIME 3 SKINCARE DOESN’T STOP AT BEDTIME $40 at bonsoiroflondon.com Harris Reed, designer: “It’s all about eye cream and a silk eye mask — these are non-negotiables.” 4 PAIN IS NOT GAIN 4 PAIN IS NOT GAIN £23 at LookFantastic Dr Richard Devine, aesthetic doctor and founder of Devine Clinic: “A product that’s working shouldn’t leave your skin feeling persistently red, sore, itchy or inflamed. Mild adjustment periods can occur with certain active ingredients, but ongoing discomfort is usually a sign that the skin barrier is becoming irritated rather than improved. If redness, burning or sensitivity continues beyond the first few uses, it’s often worth reducing frequency or reassessing whether the product is appropriate for your skin.” Advertisement - Continue Reading Below 5 DON'T LET OIL WIN 5 DON'T LET OIL WIN Now 16% Off £53 at embassyofbeauty.co.uk Ziad Halub, co-owner of Iranian-Iraqi café bistro Logma in Hackney: “After a hot and sticky day, your skin needs help. Sweat, dead skin, SPF, pollution and general city grime can build into a layer of filth. A good foaming cleanser, one that doesn’t strip the skin, is essential. You want fresh, not squeaky. I’m currently loving African Botanics’ Baobab Clay Oxygenating Cleanser.” 6 SPF IS A MUST 6 SPF IS A MUST Shop at thebeautiful.co.uk Marc Terlet, co-founder of French grooming brand Horace: “At a minimum, an effective skincare routine involves washing your face, applying moisturiser and then sunscreen. Make things easier with an SPF moisturiser but remember to reapply every couple of hours. The sun is responsible for 80 per cent of your skin ageing. Imagine how young you would look if you’d used sunscreen every day since you were 20?
